- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to underpredict upward moves; adjust forecast upward by 2–5% for next period.
- After a sharp spike in true price, model often overreacts and overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% below peak observed price for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-period, model lags in recognizing momentum; add 1–3% upward bias to forecast starting from day of sentiment shift.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in volatile periods; if 3 consecutive days show >10% price movement, apply 5–10% downward bias to next forecast.
- When sentiment is positive and price is rising, model often overestimates continuation; reduce forecast by 3–7% if sentiment remains positive for >5 days.
- If true price exceeds forecast by >10% for 2+ consecutive days, model is likely underestimating supply/demand shock; increase forecast by 5–10% for next period.
- In absence of clear sentiment signal, model defaults to historical mean; if recent 7-day average is >10% above forecast, adjust downward by 2–5% to avoid overconfidence.
